      "observations": [
        "All 13 owned paths and every changed hunk were read, including the full removed 773-line implementation, 146-line header, 114-line IDL and both complete old/new mailto tests. The landing removes both component registrations, IDL/build entries and obsolete includes. A scoped post-landing search of mail and mailnews finds no remaining nsISmtpUrl/nsIMailtoUrl or removed contract-ID references; it does not prove that external extensions or paired engine consumers never used them.",
        "The new local parser returns selected fields through ParsedMailtoFields and calls a value-returning UnescapeAndConvert. It combines repeated recipients with comma-space, body parameters with newline, and lets later HTML aliases replace earlier ones. Selected header values undergo unescaping and MIME conversion, while body/HTML receive unescaping. Unsupported names, including the retired from/followup-to/organization/reply-to/priority fields, have no assignment branch. This is code scope, not a complete RFC or security guarantee.",
        "The old wrapper parsed the retired extra fields but GetMessageContents did not pass them to production compose fields. Therefore dropping their private storage is not evidence of a newly fixed sender-spoofing vulnerability. The new tests call getParamsForMailto and observe compose-field formatting and sanitized HTML output instead of raw wrapper properties, format, URI equality or cloning. Existing identity/format ordering and valueless-token lessons are reused at their exact current scopes.",
        "The new negative test supplies from, reply-to, organization and priority, then directly asserts only the first three compose properties are empty. It supplies no followup-to parameter and has no priority assertion. Its statement that priority is not exposed contradicts the scriptable nsIMsgCompFields priority attribute at both the original and fixed revisions and its concrete getter/setter implementation. Correct the comment and add explicit intended-result coverage rather than claiming the unasserted properties were verified.",
        "All ten new Assert.equal call sites in test_mailtoURL.js have only two arguments and no expected-result message. This violates the deliberate nonempty-message review rule. A useful message should identify the URL/property and expected value; this finding is more than a missing should word. The six message-free assertion sites in test_smtpProtocols.js are existing unchanged calls, recorded separately from the ten rewritten/new mailto sites.",
        "The original SMTP URI branch uses a generic mailnews URL mutator and the fixed branch later uses direct SetSpecInternal. Both are captured as separate phases; the deleted NewSmtpURI also resolved against aBaseURI, while these new branches do not explicitly do so. The tests use absolute URLs only. Relative URI resolution, paired engine URI behavior and thread-safety effects of removing the mailto main-thread dispatch remain bounded gaps.",
        "The return-value review suggestion is concretely adopted by UnescapeAndConvert in both owned and fixed source. Its Done badge alone is not the proof. The actual summary adds ignored-parameter and negative-test claims; source and direct assertions limit those claims. Historical Try/build/branch and patch-stack application reports remain distinct from fresh execution.",
        "The C++ parser has short reason/field comments and explicit guards for valueless tokens and empty names. GetParamsForMailto retains nested URI/params/fields creation branches; early failure returns could make these local steps clearer while preserving output/error behavior. This is a scoped readability suggestion, not a formatter failure or unrelated cleanup request. The current xpcshell configuration and shared MailServices head were checked; no lint or formatter was run.",
        "The full primary 376a5a13caa60a20ada70c56ac20aac31c63cf49e2f0ac2d30d37f359f56857f retains description and comments 1–7. The author reports a clean application, Corey reports a stack conflict, the stack is resubmitted and Corey then confirms it applies cleanly. This is patch application history, not a fresh build or parser test success.",
        "D305838's actual inline asks to return the converted value instead of using an output parameter. The exact original and accepted UnescapeAndConvert do return nsCString, so adoption is source-proved. Its actual Old/New summary adds ignored fields and a negative-test claim; the code drops those parameter names, while only three properties have direct negative assertions and priority is exposed despite the new comment. Ten new assertion messages remain absent.",
        "The earlier source-only stage used public code alone. This full join adds the complete original team discussion scopes without replacing the old objects, their timestamps or reader attribution. Done, final approval, historical Try and ongoing/failed-build landing metadata do not strengthen untested field or security guarantees."
